text:
alex: Heads-up — HelioWave asked for a focused eco-sweep next week: perf/W and perf/$ across three fan curves and two ambient temps. Can we put a simple run plan together?
helio-eng: We can host on HelioWave units. Rack-level fans can be set to quiet/auto/max. Ambient temps we can emulate: 20C and 30C. Any preferred power-capping?
sophia: Let's sweep power caps [180, 220, 260]W per board. Primary workloads: 4k-gen steady streaming and a 2k-chat mixed IO load. We want throughput @95th percentile p95 latency SLAs and perf-per-dollar using our current marketplace price points.
ops: FYI ops: we'll need a Redwood engineer on-site for the handoff and to validate container signing. How many people do you need?
alex: One is fine for handover. We'll remote in for the rest.
luis: Telemetry schema request: per_gpu.power_w, per_gpu.freq_mhz, host.cpu_pct, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, perf_dollar_usd, fan_mode. JSON lines preferred to stream into our bench pipeline.
helio-eng: We can emit prometheus + JSON-lines. We'll add a tag helio_fw=<hash> and fan_mode in the metadata.
sophia: Can you also emit thermal throttling events and VRM_temp? Those explain sudden drops.
helio-eng: Yes VRM and throttles included. Note: the async memcpy kernel patch we're testing needs a small firmware tweak. If that tweak is on, older chassis may reboot under max fan=quiet at 30C. We'll need a canary run.
pm: Reboot risk noted. Can we do a canary with one chassis for each fan mode and the patch variants before full sweep?
alex: Absolutely. Canary plan: one chassis per fan_mode x both kernel variants (baseline and async-copy). If stable, proceed to full rack.
benchbot: Reminder: benchbot will parse files named `helio-*.jsonl` in /bench/artifacts and run the ingestion pipeline. Reaction: :robot_face:.
luis: Run harness snippet I'll push to repo:
```
./bench/run.sh \
  --model redwood-4k-gen:prod \
  --batch-sizes 8,16,32 \
  --power-caps 180,220,260 \
  --fan-modes quiet,auto,max \
  --ambient 20,30 \
  --out /bench/artifacts/helio-$RUN_ID.jsonl \
  --metrics jsonl \
  --retries 2
```
helio-eng: We'll provide a small helper to set fan curves via IPMI and annotate run metadata. We'll also capture rack PDU readings for total power.
sophia: For perf-per-dollar, use marketplace spot price USD/hour we agreed last quarter (repo: /pricing/marketplace-2025-q1.json). Compute perf_dollar_usd = tokens_per_sec / (price_usd_per_hour/3600).
luis: Got it. Add a field `perf_per_usd` to the JSON lines.
ops: Logistics — HelioWave has rack at their lab Mon-Wed. We should schedule Tue for main sweep, Mon for canaries. Who can be on-site Mon morning?
alex: I can do Mon 09:00-13:00 PT for canaries. Sophia can join Tue for full sweep.
pm: We'll also put a short NDA addendum for publishing joint numbers; no embargo lift until both legal teams sign.
helio-eng: Understood. We'll mark all bench outputs as partner-private until signoff.
sophia: Post-run deliverables: raw JSONL artifacts, benchbot summary, A/B plots (perf vs power, perf/W heatmap), and a short joint blog draft. Can someone volunteer to draft the blog?
luis: I can draft the technical appendix. Alex can take the summary.
alex: Happy to. I'll also create a checklist PR in the repo with run commands and expected artifact locations.
benchbot: When artifacts appear benchbot will post a summary in #partnerships and create a ticket in our bench tracker. :white_check_mark:
sophia: Final note: please ensure deterministic seed set for quality checks (20 prompts). Put them in `/bench/inputs/helio-seed-2025-03-25.json`.
luis: Seed set added.
helio-eng: All right, we'll publish firmware toggles and IPMI scripts by EOD Friday. See you on the handoff call 08:45 Mon.
alex: Thanks all 44d
